correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from RESULT.md at exact assigned Git blob. A blade center-color class of size a must satisfy a>=ceil(m/2), while a competing color class needs >=ceil(m/2)+1 vertices; this excludes mixing. Blades avoiding center color are also monochromatic. The center has nm neighbors and bm same-color neighbors, hence b>=ceil(n/2). Surjective noncenter-blade assignments give the Stirling count. Independent direct neighbor-condition exhaustive checks covered 10 (n,m,q) palette-size cases with n=1..3 and m=2..3, matching structure and counts; the universal proof is analytic.
